Archive item 2: Change Request CR-2021-014: Berth Extension at Apapa Port
Source format: Change Request

The scope of this CR is limited to civil works, fendering, and mooring hardware. It does not include dredging, lighting towers, or shore-power connections, which are covered under separate work packages (WP-04 and WP-07 respectively).

---

**2. BACKGROUND AND JUSTIFICATION**

2.1 Current berthing capacity at Apapa Port is constrained by the effective length of Berth 5, which was originally constructed in 1978 for vessels of up to 180 m LOA. The TOA baseline traffic study (ref. ATS-TOA-TS-009, Rev. C) indicates that by Q1 2023, the frequency of vessels in the 190–210 m LOA bracket will increase by 34% relative to 2019 levels, driven primarily by new container services transiting the Gulf of Guinea.

2.2 Without the extension, these larger vessels are forced to either:

- (a) berth at Tin Can Island Port (TCIP) and transfer cargo by barge, adding 12–18 hours to port stay; or
- (b) use Berth 5 with reduced under-keel clearance and restricted crane reach, which has already caused two fender failures in 2020 (incident reports IR-2020-114 and IR-2020-208).

2.3 The extension will add 60 m of usable berth length, bringing the total to 240 m, and will include two new bollards rated at 150 t and a continuous fender line compatible with the existing Yokohama-type units. This configuration will allow safe simultaneous handling of one 210 m container vessel and one 80 m tug/barge moored astern, or a single vessel of up to 240 m.

2.4 ATS conducted a site survey on 17–18 August 2021 (survey log ref. ATS-SV-2021-044) to verify seabed conditions along the proposed extension line. The survey confirmed an average water depth of 11.4 m CD at the berth face, with no buried utilities or abandoned mooring anchors within the footprint. Two concrete pile stubs from an abandoned 1960s dolphin were found and will require removal as part of the works.

Vessels currently allocated to Berth 5 will be temporarily re-allocated to Berths 3 and 4, which have sufficient capacity to absorb the additional traffic based on the 2021 Q3 berth utilisation report.

   crane availability constraints.

2) **Throughput growth**: Container traffic through Apapa Wharf grew by 18% year-on-year
   between 2020 and 2021, and the trend has continued into 2022. Without additional lifting
   capacity, the terminal risks losing transshipment business to competing West African ports.

3) **Operational redundancy**: The current fleet has no spare crane capacity. Any unscheduled
   maintenance event immediately reduces throughput by 25%. The two additional cranes will
   provide necessary redundancy and allow the maintenance schedule to be brought back to
   manufacturer-recommended intervals.

4) **Dwell time reduction**: Average container dwell time currently stands at 9.6 days,
   against the LPA target of 7 days. Additional crane capacity will directly reduce yard
   congestion and improve truck turnaround times.

5) **Regulatory compliance**: NIMASA guidelines on port efficiency (NIMASA/OP/2021/88)
   require the terminal to demonstrate progressive improvement in vessel turnaround metrics.
   The proposed upgrade supports compliance with these guidelines.

**5. Interface with Existing Operations**

The installation programme has been coordinated with the terminal's 2022 maintenance shutdown
window (scheduled 12–19 December 2022) to minimise disruption. Civil works on the runway
extension shall be undertaken in two phases, with each phase limited to a 120-metre section so
that at least three cranes remain operational at all times.
The ATS engineering team notes that the difference between the lowest quote (Vendor B) and the ATS cost estimation is approximately USD 250,000. This variance is primarily attributable to the inclusion of civil works and the cost of the anti-collision interface with the existing fleet, which Vendor B's quote does not cover. A detailed technical evaluation matrix is being prepared and will be presented to the LPA technical committee alongside the final vendor selection recommendation.

**8. Budget and Funding Sources**

The total estimated cost of USD 1,800,000 is to be funded as follows:

1. **LPA Capital Expenditure Allocation (2022/2023 fiscal year):** USD 1,200,000 has been provisionally earmarked in the current capital budget under the equipment modernisation line item. This allocation is subject to final approval by the LPA board in the upcoming budget review meeting scheduled for 28 July 2022.

2. **Terminal Revenue Reserve:** The remaining USD 600,000 is to be drawn from the terminal's internally generated revenue reserve, which has been set aside for infrastructure improvements. The finance department has confirmed the availability of these funds.

A formal request for the release of the LPA allocation will be submitted immediately upon approval of this change request. The procurement timeline assumes that funds will be available by 15 August 2022 to enable the placement of the order and secure the quoted delivery slot.

**9. Implementation Timeline and Milestones**

Change Request CR-2022-006 estimates an estimated_cost of 1800000 USD. Record status: pending verification.

The proposed implementation timeline is aligned with the operational constraints of the terminal and the 2022 maintenance shutdown window. Key milestones are as follows:

| Milestone | Target Date |
|---|---|
| Approval of Change Request CR-2022-006 | 30 June 2022 |
| Final vendor selection and contract award | 15 August 2022 |
| Commencement of civil works – Phase 1 (120m section) | 3 October 2022 |
| Completion of Phase 1 civil works | 30 October 2022 |
| Commencement of Phase 2 civil works (120m section) | 7 November 2022 |
| Planned maintenance shutdown window | 12–19 December 2022 |
| Delivery of cranes to Apapa Wharf | 15 January 2023 |
| Installation and commissioning of Crane 1 | 28 February 2023 |
| Installation and commissioning of Crane 2 | 15 March 2023 |
| Full operational handover and training completion | 31 March 2023 |

This timeline is contingent upon the timely release of funds and the delivery schedule of the selected vendor. The 12–19 December 2022 shutdown window will be used to complete the critical interface connections between the new crane runway and the existing power supply, minimising disruption to normal operations.

**10. Risk Assessment and Mitigation**

The following risks have been identified and mitigation measures proposed:

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delay in fund release beyond 15 August 2022 | Medium | High – delays vendor order and entire schedule | Finance to prioritise release; escalate to LPA board if required |
| Vendor B's lack of local service network | Medium | Medium – potential downtime if breakdown occurs | Negotiate a service level agreement with a third-party maintenance provider in Lagos |
| Civil works overrun due to unforeseen ground conditions | Medium | Medium – may delay crane installation | Geotechnical survey of runway area has been commissioned and will be completed before contract award |
| Import duty waiver not granted | Low | High – adds approx. USD 180,000 to cost | Engage with NPA and Nigerian Customs Service early; alternative is to absorb cost from contingency |
| Delays at Apapa Wharf for offloading of cranes | Medium | Medium – affects installation start date | Coordinate with terminal operations to reserve a berth window; use a specialised heavy-lift vessel |
**CHANGE REQUEST CR-2022-006: EQUIPMENT UPGRADE – ADDITIONAL GANTRY CRANES**

**11. Installation and Commissioning Plan**

The installation and commissioning of the two additional gantry cranes will be undertaken in accordance with the manufacturer’s specifications and the approved method statement. The detailed plan is provided below:

**11.1 Pre-Installation Activities**

Prior to the arrival of the cranes at Apapa Wharf, the following preparatory activities will be completed:

- Verification of the civil works and runway alignment against the approved drawings.
- Load testing of the crane runway and power supply connections.
- Mobilisation of the installation contractor and delivery of all necessary tooling and lifting equipment.
- Confirmation of the availability of the heavy-lift vessel berthing window with terminal operations.

**11.2 Installation Sequence**

The installation sequence for each crane is as follows:

| Activity | Duration | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Offloading of crane components from vessel | 2 days | Vendor / Terminal Operations |
| Assembly of main structural components | 5 days | Vendor Installation Team |
| Electrical and control system installation | 4 days | Vendor Electrical Engineers |
| Mechanical alignment and torqueing | 3 days | Vendor / LPA Mechanical Team |
| Functional testing of individual systems | 2 days | Vendor / LPA Technical Committee |
| Load testing and certification | 2 days | NIMASA / Accredited Inspector |
| Final commissioning and handover | 1 day | Vendor / LPA |

The installation of Crane 1 will commence immediately upon completion of the offloading and will be completed within 21 working days. Following the commissioning of Crane 1, the installation team will move to Crane 2, with a similar 21-working-day programme. The two cranes will not be installed concurrently to allow the operations team to retain the use of the existing gantry crane throughout the installation period.

**11.3 Commissioning and Testing**

Commissioning will be performed in phases to ensure that all safety systems operate correctly and that the cranes meet the operational requirements of the port. The commissioning protocol will include:

- No-load operational tests of all motions (hoist, trolley, and gantry travel).
- Full-load tests at 100% and 110% of rated capacity.
- Testing of all safety interlocks, limit switches, and emergency stop systems.
- Verification of the anti-collision system between the new cranes and the existing crane.
- Performance of a 24-hour continuous running test to identify any reliability issues.

All testing will be witnessed by the LPA Technical Committee and a representative of NIMASA. A certificate of compliance will be issued upon successful completion of the load tests.

**11.4 Operational Handover**

Operational handover will occur in two stages:

1. **Stage 1 – Provisional Handover:** Following successful commissioning of each crane, the crane will be made available for operations under the supervision of the vendor’s commissioning team. This stage will last for a period of 14 days.
2. **Stage 2 – Final Handover:** After the 14-day provisional period, and upon completion of all rectification works identified during the provisional period, the crane will be formally handed over to LPA operations. Final handover will be accompanied by the submission of all documentation, including as-built drawings, maintenance manuals, and certification.

**12. Training Plan**

A comprehensive training programme will be provided by the vendor for LPA operational and maintenance staff. The training will cover:

- Safe operation of the gantry cranes, including load handling and stacking procedures.
- Routine pre-operational checks and daily inspection routines.
- Basic maintenance and troubleshooting of mechanical and electrical systems.
- Use of the crane’s onboard diagnostic systems.
- Emergency procedures, including load recovery and crane shutdown.

Chief Emeka Okafor presented the LPA position. He tabled a cost breakdown showing:

- Increase in marine diesel cost by an average of 18% between January and November 2023.
- Replacement parts for two gantry cranes (Nos. 3 and 7) due to extended usage.
- Additional security personnel deployed at the Tin Can Island gate since March 2023.
- Maintenance dredging of the berth pockets carried out in September 2023.

He proposed a new tariff of ₦54,500 per TEU, effective 1 January 2024.

**4.2 ATS Position**

Alhaji Suleiman Bello responded on behalf of ATS. He acknowledged the cost pressures but noted that ATS had absorbed certain charges in the past and that the volume of transshipment cargo had declined by roughly 6% in the third quarter. He argued that a steep increase would discourage shipping lines from routing cargo through Lagos, especially when compared with Cotonou and Tema. ATS proposed a tariff of ₦49,800 per TEU.

**4.3 Joint Consideration**

The parties discussed the gap between the two proposals. The following points were raised:

- The need to maintain a stable and predictable tariff for the 2024 budget cycle.
- The impact of the tariff on the total landed cost of goods, particularly for essential commodities such as rice, sugar, and fertiliser.
- The requirement to align with any applicable NPA guidelines on port service charges.
- The possibility of a phased implementation, should a single rate not be agreed.

Mrs. Ngozi Umeh noted that ATS had budgeted for a mid-range figure and that an agreement above ₦50,000 per TEU would require a board approval at ATS, which could be obtained by the end of the year.

Mr. Tunde Bakare queried whether the tariff would apply uniformly to both laden and empty containers. The Chairperson responded that the tariff under discussion applied to laden containers only, with empties remaining at the existing rate of ₦12,500 per TEU, subject to a separate review.

**4.4 Breakout Session**

The meeting went into a brief breakout session at 12:20 hrs. The LPA team (Mrs. Adeyemi, Chief Okafor, Mr. Bakare) and the ATS team (Alhaji Bello, Mrs. Umeh, Ms. Nwosu) deliberated separately. Upon reconvening at 12:50 hrs, both sides indicated a willingness to meet in the middle.

---

After further deliberation, the parties reached an agreement. The following was recorded as the outcome of the meeting:

**Negotiation Note NN-2023-002 records a negotiated_tariff_per_teu of 52000 NGN. Record status: current.**

This rate is the current and binding tariff for laden containers, effective from 1 January 2024. It supersedes the previous rate of ₦47,200 per TEU, which was applicable until 31 December 2023.

The tariff shall apply to all laden container movements (import and export) at both Apapa and Tin Can Island terminals operated by ATS under the terms of the existing concession agreement.

---

**6.0 OTHER MATTERS**

**6.1 Empty Containers**

As noted in section 4.3, the rate for empty containers remains unchanged at ₦12,500 per TEU. A review of this rate may be initiated by either party in the second quarter of 2024.

**6.2 Tariff Review Mechanism**

The parties agreed to establish a joint tariff review committee, to be co-chaired by Chief Emeka Okafor (LPA) and Mrs. Ngozi Umeh (ATS). The committee shall meet every six months to review cost indices and throughput data. Any adjustment to the tariff shall be made by mutual written agreement.

**6.3 Payment Terms**

Payment terms remain unchanged. All charges are payable within 14 days of invoice. The existing provision for a 2% discount for payment within 7 days shall continue.

**APPENDIX B: IMPLEMENTATION PLAN AND FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS**

The following implementation plan was agreed at the meeting and is recorded here for the avoidance of doubt. It sets out the responsibilities of each party and the timelines for the actions arising from the tariff revision. The plan is without prejudice to the obligations set out in the body of this Negotiation Note.

**B1. Billing System Updates**

1. LPA shall, by not later than 15 February 2024, update its billing and invoicing systems to reflect the revised tariff. The update shall be applied prospectively from 1 July 2023, and LPA shall ensure that no invoice issued after the date of this Note is raised at the old tariff rates.
2. ATS shall by the same date update its customer billing records and any internal systems used to calculate charges payable to LPA, so as to align with the revised tariff.
3. Both parties shall conduct a joint dry-run of the updated systems during the week commencing 19 February 2024 to confirm that the revised rates are correctly applied to sample invoices. The dry-run results shall be shared by 23 February 2024.

**B2. Public Circular and Stakeholder Notification**

1. LPA shall issue a public circular announcing the revised tariff on or before 1 March 2024. The circular shall state the effective date of 1 July 2023, the new rates, and the procedure for customers to claim refunds or credit notes where they were overcharged during the transition period.
2. ATS shall, within five working days of the circular being issued, notify its customers directly by email and by notice displayed at its operational offices at Tin Can Island and Apapa Wharf. The notification shall include a copy of the circular and a summary of the refund/credit note procedure.
3. The parties shall jointly prepare a frequently asked questions (FAQ) document to accompany the circular. The FAQ shall be approved by both parties by 28 February 2024.

**B3. Compliance Reporting and Verification Audit**

1. ATS shall provide LPA with a compliance report by 31 March 2024, confirming that all invoices raised after 1 July 2023 have been adjusted to reflect the revised tariff. The report shall include a schedule of all refunds or credit notes issued to customers who were overcharged during the transition period, together with the total value of such refunds/credit notes.
2. LPA shall conduct a verification audit of ATS billing records for the period July 2023 to March 2024. The audit shall be completed by 30 April 2024. LPA shall provide ATS with a draft audit report for comment within seven days of completion, and the final audit report shall be issued by 15 May 2024.
3. Any discrepancies identified during the audit shall be resolved jointly within fourteen days of the final audit report being issued. If the parties are unable to resolve a discrepancy, the matter shall be referred to the joint tariff review committee at its first meeting.

**B4. Joint Tariff Review Committee**

1. The inaugural meeting of the joint tariff review committee shall be held in June 2024. The committee shall comprise two representatives from each party, to be nominated by the respective Managing Directors by 15 May 2024.
2. The committee shall consider cost indices and throughput data for the first half of 2024, and shall make recommendations to the parties on whether any adjustment to the tariff is warranted. The committee shall report its recommendations by 31 July 2024.
3. The committee shall meet at least twice a year thereafter, or more frequently if either party requests a meeting in writing.

**B5. Review of Empty Container Tariff**

1. In accordance with Section 6.1 of this Note, the empty container tariff shall be reviewed in July 2024. The review shall be conducted by the joint tariff review committee, which shall consider data on empty container movements, storage durations, and the costs incurred by LPA in handling empty containers.
2. The committee shall submit its recommendations on the empty container tariff to the parties by 31 July 2024. Any revised empty container tariff shall take effect from 1 October 2024, subject to the agreement of both parties.

ARTICLE 6: DISPUTE RESOLUTION

6.1 **Governing Law.** This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

6.2 **Amicable Settlement.** The Parties shall use reasonable endeavours to settle any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, or the breach, termination, or invalidity thereof, through friendly negotiations. Either Party may initiate such negotiations by written notice to the other Party, and the Parties shall meet within fourteen (14) days of such notice to discuss and seek a resolution.

6.3 **Expert Determination.** If the dispute relates to a technical or operational matter, including but not limited to the interpretation of the Tariff Schedule, berth allocation, or the application of the Minimum Performance Standards, the Parties may, by mutual agreement in writing, refer the dispute to an independent expert. The expert shall be appointed by the Parties, or failing agreement within fourteen (14) days, by the President of the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators (Nigeria Branch). The expert shall act as an expert and not as an arbitrator, and the expert's determination shall be final and binding on the Parties save in the case of manifest error or fraud.

6.4 **Arbitration.** Subject to Clause 6.2 and 6.3, any dispute arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, including any question regarding its existence, validity, or termination, which remains unresolved for a period of thirty (30) days from the date of the notice under Clause 6.2, shall be referred to and finally resolved by arbitration in accordance with the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, Cap A18, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004, as amended or re-enacted from time to time.

(a) The arbitral tribunal shall consist of three (3) arbitrators. Each Party shall appoint one (1) arbitrator, and the two (2) arbitrators so appointed shall appoint the third arbitrator, who shall act as the presiding arbitrator. If a Party fails to appoint an arbitrator within thirty (30) days of receipt of a written request from the other Party to do so, or if the two (2) arbitrators fail to agree on the presiding arbitrator within thirty (30) days of their appointment, the appointment shall be made by the President of the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators (Nigeria Branch) upon the application of either Party.

(b) The seat of arbitration shall be Lagos, Nigeria, and the language of the arbitration shall be English.

(c) The award of the arbitral tribunal shall be final and binding upon the Parties, and judgment upon the award may be entered in any court of competent jurisdiction.

6.5 **Continuity of Obligations.** Unless otherwise agreed in writing, the existence of a dispute shall not entitle either Party to suspend the performance of its obligations under this Agreement, and each Party shall continue to perform its obligations pending the resolution of the dispute in accordance with this Article 6.

ARTICLE 7: TERMINATION

7.1 **Term.** Subject to the provisions of this Article 7, this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and, unless terminated earlier in accordance with its terms, shall continue in full force and effect for a period of twenty (20) years from the Effective Date (the "Term"). Upon expiry of the Term, this Agreement shall terminate automatically without any further act or notice by either Party.

7.2 **Termination for Convenience.** LPA may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time after the tenth (10th) anniversary of the Effective Date by giving ATS not less than twelve (12) months' prior written notice of such termination. In the event of such termination, LPA shall pay to ATS a sum equal to the unamortised capital expenditure incurred by ATS in respect of the Terminal as at the date of termination, calculated in accordance with the depreciation schedule set out in Schedule 4, provided that such sum shall not exceed the aggregate of the amounts set out in the Financial Model.

The scope of this CR is limited to civil works, fendering, and mooring hardware. It does not include dredging, lighting towers, or shore-power connections, which are covered under separate work packages (WP-04 and WP-07 respectively).

---

**2. BACKGROUND AND JUSTIFICATION**

2.1 Current berthing capacity at Apapa Port is constrained by the effective length of Berth 5, which was originally constructed in 1978 for vessels of up to 180 m LOA. The TOA baseline traffic study (ref. ATS-TOA-TS-009, Rev. C) indicates that by Q1 2023, the frequency of vessels in the 190–210 m LOA bracket will increase by 34% relative to 2019 levels, driven primarily by new container services transiting the Gulf of Guinea.

2.2 Without the extension, these larger vessels are forced to either:

- (a) berth at Tin Can Island Port (TCIP) and transfer cargo by barge, adding 12–18 hours to port stay; or
- (b) use Berth 5 with reduced under-keel clearance and restricted crane reach, which has already caused two fender failures in 2020 (incident reports IR-2020-114 and IR-2020-208).

2.3 The extension will add 60 m of usable berth length, bringing the total to 240 m, and will include two new bollards rated at 150 t and a continuous fender line compatible with the existing Yokohama-type units. This configuration will allow safe simultaneous handling of one 210 m container vessel and one 80 m tug/barge moored astern, or a single vessel of up to 240 m.

2.4 ATS conducted a site survey on 17–18 August 2021 (survey log ref. ATS-SV-2021-044) to verify seabed conditions along the proposed extension line. The survey confirmed an average water depth of 11.4 m CD at the berth face, with no buried utilities or abandoned mooring anchors within the footprint. Two concrete pile stubs from an abandoned 1960s dolphin were found and will require removal as part of the works.

**4. Justification**

The justification for the installation of two additional gantry cranes is as follows:

Change Request CR-2022-006 describes a scope_description of installation of two additional gantry cranes. Record status: current.

1) **Capacity constraint**: The existing four cranes cannot cope with peak-hour demand.
   Vessel waiting time at anchorage averaged 3.2 days in May 2022, directly attributable to
   crane availability constraints.

2) **Throughput growth**: Container traffic through Apapa Wharf grew by 18% year-on-year
   between 2020 and 2021, and the trend has continued into 2022. Without additional lifting
   capacity, the terminal risks losing transshipment business to competing West African ports.

3) **Operational redundancy**: The current fleet has no spare crane capacity. Any unscheduled
   maintenance event immediately reduces throughput by 25%. The two additional cranes will
   provide necessary redundancy and allow the maintenance schedule to be brought back to
   manufacturer-recommended intervals.

4) **Dwell time reduction**: Average container dwell time currently stands at 9.6 days,
   against the LPA target of 7 days. Additional crane capacity will directly reduce yard
   congestion and improve truck turnaround times.

5) **Regulatory compliance**: NIMASA guidelines on port efficiency (NIMASA/OP/2021/88)
   require the terminal to demonstrate progressive improvement in vessel turnaround metrics.
   The proposed upgrade supports compliance with these guidelines.

The installation programme has been coordinated with the terminal's 2022 maintenance shutdown
window (scheduled 12–19 December 2022) to minimise disruption. Civil works on the runway
extension shall be undertaken in two phases, with each phase limited to a 120-metre section so
that at least three cranes remain operational at all times.

**CHANGE REQUEST CR-2022-006: EQUIPMENT UPGRADE – ADDITIONAL GANTRY CRANES**

**11. Installation and Commissioning Plan**

The installation and commissioning of the two additional gantry cranes will be undertaken in accordance with the manufacturer’s specifications and the approved method statement. The detailed plan is provided below:

**11.1 Pre-Installation Activities**

Prior to the arrival of the cranes at Apapa Wharf, the following preparatory activities will be completed:

- Verification of the civil works and runway alignment against the approved drawings.
- Load testing of the crane runway and power supply connections.
- Mobilisation of the installation contractor and delivery of all necessary tooling and lifting equipment.
- Confirmation of the availability of the heavy-lift vessel berthing window with terminal operations.

**11.2 Installation Sequence**

The installation sequence for each crane is as follows:

| Activity | Duration | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Offloading of crane components from vessel | 2 days | Vendor / Terminal Operations |
| Assembly of main structural components | 5 days | Vendor Installation Team |
| Electrical and control system installation | 4 days | Vendor Electrical Engineers |
| Mechanical alignment and torqueing | 3 days | Vendor / LPA Mechanical Team |
| Functional testing of individual systems | 2 days | Vendor / LPA Technical Committee |
| Load testing and certification | 2 days | NIMASA / Accredited Inspector |
| Final commissioning and handover | 1 day | Vendor / LPA |

The installation of Crane 1 will commence immediately upon completion of the offloading and will be completed within 21 working days. Following the commissioning of Crane 1, the installation team will move to Crane 2, with a similar 21-working-day programme. The two cranes will not be installed concurrently to allow the operations team to retain the use of the existing gantry crane throughout the installation period.

**11.3 Commissioning and Testing**

Commissioning will be performed in phases to ensure that all safety systems operate correctly and that the cranes meet the operational requirements of the port. The commissioning protocol will include:

- No-load operational tests of all motions (hoist, trolley, and gantry travel).
- Full-load tests at 100% and 110% of rated capacity.
- Testing of all safety interlocks, limit switches, and emergency stop systems.
- Verification of the anti-collision system between the new cranes and the existing crane.
- Performance of a 24-hour continuous running test to identify any reliability issues.

All testing will be witnessed by the LPA Technical Committee and a representative of NIMASA. A certificate of compliance will be issued upon successful completion of the load tests.

**11.4 Operational Handover**

Operational handover will occur in two stages:

1. **Stage 1 – Provisional Handover:** Following successful commissioning of each crane, the crane will be made available for operations under the supervision of the vendor’s commissioning team. This stage will last for a period of 14 days.
2. **Stage 2 – Final Handover:** After the 14-day provisional period, and upon completion of all rectification works identified during the provisional period, the crane will be formally handed over to LPA operations. Final handover will be accompanied by the submission of all documentation, including as-built drawings, maintenance manuals, and certification.

**12. Training Plan**

A comprehensive training programme will be provided by the vendor for LPA operational and maintenance staff. The training will cover:

- Safe operation of the gantry cranes, including load handling and stacking procedures.
- Routine pre-operational checks and daily inspection routines.
- Basic maintenance and troubleshooting of mechanical and electrical systems.
- Use of the crane’s onboard diagnostic systems.
- Emergency procedures, including load recovery and crane shutdown.

documents.title: Negotiation Note NN-2023-002: Tariff Revision Meeting
documents.content:
Chief Emeka Okafor presented the LPA position. He tabled a cost breakdown showing:

- Increase in marine diesel cost by an average of 18% between January and November 2023.
- Replacement parts for two gantry cranes (Nos. 3 and 7) due to extended usage.
- Additional security personnel deployed at the Tin Can Island gate since March 2023.
- Maintenance dredging of the berth pockets carried out in September 2023.

He proposed a new tariff of ₦54,500 per TEU, effective 1 January 2024.

**4.2 ATS Position**

Alhaji Suleiman Bello responded on behalf of ATS. He acknowledged the cost pressures but noted that ATS had absorbed certain charges in the past and that the volume of transshipment cargo had declined by roughly 6% in the third quarter. He argued that a steep increase would discourage shipping lines from routing cargo through Lagos, especially when compared with Cotonou and Tema. ATS proposed a tariff of ₦49,800 per TEU.

**4.3 Joint Consideration**

The parties discussed the gap between the two proposals. The following points were raised:

- The need to maintain a stable and predictable tariff for the 2024 budget cycle.
- The impact of the tariff on the total landed cost of goods, particularly for essential commodities such as rice, sugar, and fertiliser.
- The requirement to align with any applicable NPA guidelines on port service charges.
- The possibility of a phased implementation, should a single rate not be agreed.

Mrs. Ngozi Umeh noted that ATS had budgeted for a mid-range figure and that an agreement above ₦50,000 per TEU would require a board approval at ATS, which could be obtained by the end of the year.

Mr. Tunde Bakare queried whether the tariff would apply uniformly to both laden and empty containers. The Chairperson responded that the tariff under discussion applied to laden containers only, with empties remaining at the existing rate of ₦12,500 per TEU, subject to a separate review.

**4.4 Breakout Session**

The meeting went into a brief breakout session at 12:20 hrs. The LPA team (Mrs. Adeyemi, Chief Okafor, Mr. Bakare) and the ATS team (Alhaji Bello, Mrs. Umeh, Ms. Nwosu) deliberated separately. Upon reconvening at 12:50 hrs, both sides indicated a willingness to meet in the middle.

---

**5.0 AGREED OUTCOME**

After further deliberation, the parties reached an agreement. The following was recorded as the outcome of the meeting:

**Negotiation Note NN-2023-002 records a negotiated_tariff_per_teu of 52000 NGN. Record status: current.**

This rate is the current and binding tariff for laden containers, effective from 1 January 2024. It supersedes the previous rate of ₦47,200 per TEU, which was applicable until 31 December 2023.

The tariff shall apply to all laden container movements (import and export) at both Apapa and Tin Can Island terminals operated by ATS under the terms of the existing concession agreement.

---

**6.0 OTHER MATTERS**

**6.1 Empty Containers**

As noted in section 4.3, the rate for empty containers remains unchanged at ₦12,500 per TEU. A review of this rate may be initiated by either party in the second quarter of 2024.

**6.2 Tariff Review Mechanism**

The parties agreed to establish a joint tariff review committee, to be co-chaired by Chief Emeka Okafor (LPA) and Mrs. Ngozi Umeh (ATS). The committee shall meet every six months to review cost indices and throughput data. Any adjustment to the tariff shall be made by mutual written agreement.

**6.3 Payment Terms**

Payment terms remain unchanged. All charges are payable within 14 days of invoice. The existing provision for a 2% discount for payment within 7 days shall continue.

**APPENDIX B: IMPLEMENTATION PLAN AND FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS**

The following implementation plan was agreed at the meeting and is recorded here for the avoidance of doubt. It sets out the responsibilities of each party and the timelines for the actions arising from the tariff revision. The plan is without prejudice to the obligations set out in the body of this Negotiation Note.

**B1. Billing System Updates**

1. LPA shall, by not later than 15 February 2024, update its billing and invoicing systems to reflect the revised tariff. The update shall be applied prospectively from 1 July 2023, and LPA shall ensure that no invoice issued after the date of this Note is raised at the old tariff rates.
2. ATS shall by the same date update its customer billing records and any internal systems used to calculate charges payable to LPA, so as to align with the revised tariff.
3. Both parties shall conduct a joint dry-run of the updated systems during the week commencing 19 February 2024 to confirm that the revised rates are correctly applied to sample invoices. The dry-run results shall be shared by 23 February 2024.

**B2. Public Circular and Stakeholder Notification**

1. LPA shall issue a public circular announcing the revised tariff on or before 1 March 2024. The circular shall state the effective date of 1 July 2023, the new rates, and the procedure for customers to claim refunds or credit notes where they were overcharged during the transition period.
2. ATS shall, within five working days of the circular being issued, notify its customers directly by email and by notice displayed at its operational offices at Tin Can Island and Apapa Wharf. The notification shall include a copy of the circular and a summary of the refund/credit note procedure.
3. The parties shall jointly prepare a frequently asked questions (FAQ) document to accompany the circular. The FAQ shall be approved by both parties by 28 February 2024.

**B3. Compliance Reporting and Verification Audit**

1. ATS shall provide LPA with a compliance report by 31 March 2024, confirming that all invoices raised after 1 July 2023 have been adjusted to reflect the revised tariff. The report shall include a schedule of all refunds or credit notes issued to customers who were overcharged during the transition period, together with the total value of such refunds/credit notes.
2. LPA shall conduct a verification audit of ATS billing records for the period July 2023 to March 2024. The audit shall be completed by 30 April 2024. LPA shall provide ATS with a draft audit report for comment within seven days of completion, and the final audit report shall be issued by 15 May 2024.
3. Any discrepancies identified during the audit shall be resolved jointly within fourteen days of the final audit report being issued. If the parties are unable to resolve a discrepancy, the matter shall be referred to the joint tariff review committee at its first meeting.

**B4. Joint Tariff Review Committee**

1. The inaugural meeting of the joint tariff review committee shall be held in June 2024. The committee shall comprise two representatives from each party, to be nominated by the respective Managing Directors by 15 May 2024.
2. The committee shall consider cost indices and throughput data for the first half of 2024, and shall make recommendations to the parties on whether any adjustment to the tariff is warranted. The committee shall report its recommendations by 31 July 2024.
3. The committee shall meet at least twice a year thereafter, or more frequently if either party requests a meeting in writing.

**B5. Review of Empty Container Tariff**

1. In accordance with Section 6.1 of this Note, the empty container tariff shall be reviewed in July 2024. The review shall be conducted by the joint tariff review committee, which shall consider data on empty container movements, storage durations, and the costs incurred by LPA in handling empty containers.
2. The committee shall submit its recommendations on the empty container tariff to the parties by 31 July 2024. Any revised empty container tariff shall take effect from 1 October 2024, subject to the agreement of both parties.
